transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my face. Specifically, the left side of it. 

It just looks really crooked and messed up to me. It's basically all I think about. Like, when I'm at work at the warehouse, or if I go out to salsa night, I just feel like everyone is staring at it and noticing how off it is. People tell me they don't see anything when I bring it up, but... I just can't stop focusing on it, and it's really getting to me.
When people tell you they do not see anything wrong, can you consider that your perception might be mistaken, or are you completely convinced that the left side of your face is crooked?

I... I mean, I hear them when they say that. But I just can't believe it. Like, I look in the mirror and it's right there. It's so obvious to me. So, no, I don't really think I'm mistaken. I'm pretty much convinced it's crooked, no matter what anyone else says. It's just hard to ignore what I see with my own eyes.
Do you repeatedly check the left side of your face in mirrors or photographs because of this concern?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially at work. Like, before I go back out on the inventory floor, I'll go to the bathroom and I just keep checking my face in the mirror. 

I end up standing there fixing my cap, trying to make it look right, and just rubbing at the exact same spot on my face. I do it so much that I lose track of time. Sometimes I'm so late getting back from doing it that my picking numbers fall behind, and then my boss gets on me about it again. So, yeah, I check it a lot.
When you check or adjust your face, does it give you temporary relief from the worry?

Um, no, not really. I don't think it gives me any relief. 

I just feel like I have to do it, you know? But it doesn't make the worry go away at all. I usually just leave the bathroom feeling just as bad about it, if not worse, because I just spent all that time staring at it. So, yeah, it doesn't really help.
When thoughts about your face come up, do they feel unwanted and intrusive, and do you try to resist or dismiss them?

I don't really try to push them away or anything. I mean, I guess they're unwanted because I don't really want to be stressing about my face all day at work, but... I don't try to fight the thoughts. 

It's more like it's just what I'm focused on, because to me, it's a real problem. So, no, I wouldn't say I try to resist or dismiss them. They're just always kind of there.
Apart from your concern about the left side of your face, do you have any other beliefs that people say are untrue but that you remain convinced are true?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my face is the only thing I'm really focused on. People might say it's not a big deal or whatever, but I don't have anything else going on like that. Just this one thing that bothers me.
Is your main concern that the left side of your face looks unattractive or abnormal in appearance, rather than that you have a medical or physical condition affecting it?

Yeah, exactly. I'm not worried about having some disease or anything like that. It's just... I can't stop thinking about how the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. It's just really unattractive. I feel like everyone at the warehouse is looking at it, or when I go out to salsa night, people are noticing it. Even when people tell me they don't see anything, I just know it looks wrong. That's really the whole thing I'm worried about.
